spec: Write a function that collapses runs of consecutive equal elements in a list into a single element, only comparing each element to its immediate predecessor (non-adjacent duplicates are left alone). The input may contain integers or strings and may be empty.

Write a function that takes a list of integers and a positive integer n, and returns a new list containing only the elements from the input list that are evenly divisible by n, preserving order. Zero is considered a multiple of every positive n. The input list may be empty.

Write a function that takes a list of strings and a minimum length, and returns a new list containing only the strings whose length is greater than or equal to that minimum, preserving order. The input list may be empty and the minimum length may be zero.

Write a function that removes from a list every element that is None, or that is a string, list, tuple, or dict with zero length, while keeping all other values (including 0, 0.0, and False) and preserving order. The input list may contain a mix of types and may be empty.

Write a function that splits a list into consecutive chunks of a given size k, returning a list of chunks. The last chunk may contain fewer than k elements if the list length is not a multiple of k. Assume k is a positive integer; the input list may be empty.

Write a function that splits a list into consecutive chunks of a given size k, and if the final chunk has fewer than k elements, pads it on the right with a given pad value until it reaches length k. Assume k is a positive integer; the input list may be empty, in which case the result is an empty list.

Write a function that splits a list into exactly n contiguous parts that are as equal in size as possible, where any leftover elements are distributed one at a time to the earliest parts. If n is larger than the list length, some parts will be empty. Assume n is a positive integer.
Write a function that returns all contiguous windows of length k from a list, in order, as a list of sublists. If k is not a positive integer at most the length of the list, return an empty list.

Write a function that returns the sum of each contiguous window of length k from a list, in order, as a list of numbers. If k is not a positive integer at most the length of the list, return an empty list.

Write a function that returns the maximum value within each contiguous window of length k from a list, in order, as a list of numbers. If k is not a positive integer at most the length of the list, return an empty list.

Write a function that returns the running (cumulative) minimum of a list of numbers as a new list of the same length, where each output element is the smallest input value seen up to and including that position. An empty input produces an empty output.

Write a function that returns the running (cumulative) average of a list of numbers as a new list of the same length, where each output element is the average of all input elements up to and including that position, rounded to 4 decimal places. An empty input produces an empty output.

Write a function that rotates a list to the right by k positions, where elements shifted off the back reappear at the front, preserving relative order. k is a non-negative integer that may exceed the list length (use k modulo the length). An empty list rotated by any k returns an empty list.

Write a function that interleaves two lists of equal length into one list, alternating elements starting with the first list: a[0], b[0], a[1], b[1], and so on. Assume both input lists always have the same length, including possibly both being empty.

Write a function that interleaves two lists of possibly different lengths, alternating elements starting with the first list, and appends any remaining elements from the longer list at the end once the shorter list is exhausted. Either input list may be empty.

Write a function that splits a list of integers into two lists: one containing the even numbers and one containing the odd numbers, each preserving their relative order from the input, and returns them as a tuple (evens, odds). Negative numbers follow standard Python even/odd rules. The input may be empty.

Write a function that takes a list of numbers and a threshold, and splits it into two lists: one with elements strictly less than the threshold and one with elements greater than or equal to it, each preserving relative order, returned as a tuple (below, at_or_above). The input list may be empty.

Write a function that takes an arbitrarily nested list (lists inside lists to any depth) and returns a single flat list containing all the non-list elements in the same left-to-right order they appear. The input may contain no nesting at all, or may be empty.

Write a function that returns a list of the differences between each element and the one before it in the input list: result[i] = lst[i+1] - lst[i]. The result has one fewer element than the input. If the input has 0 or 1 elements, return an empty list.
Write a function that returns the length of the longest run of consecutive equal elements in a list. An empty list has a longest run length of 0.

Write a function that returns the length of the longest run of consecutive strictly increasing elements in a list. A single element counts as a run of length 1. An empty list has a longest run length of 0.

Write a function that returns the length of the longest run of consecutive strictly decreasing elements in a list. A single element counts as a run of length 1. An empty list has a longest run length of 0.
Write a function that returns the index of the first element in a list that is greater than or equal to a given target value, or -1 if no such element exists. The input list may be empty.
Write a function that returns the index of the last element in a list that is less than or equal to a given target value, or -1 if no such element exists. The input list may be empty.
Write a function that returns a list of all indices at which a given value occurs in a list, in ascending order. If the value does not occur, return an empty list. The input list may be empty.

Write a function that moves every occurrence of a given value to the front of the list, preserving the relative order of those occurrences and the relative order of the remaining elements, which follow after. The input list may be empty or contain no occurrences of the value.

Write a function that splits a list into consecutive chunks of a given size k (the last chunk may be smaller), reverses the elements within each chunk, and concatenates the reversed chunks back together in their original chunk order. Assume k is a positive integer; the input list may be empty.

Write a function that splits a list into consecutive sublists at the given sorted list of split points (each split point is an index where a new sublist begins), returning a list of sublists that concatenate back to the original list. If the indices list is empty, return the whole list as the single sublist.

Write a function that returns the union of two lists as a single list of unique values, preserving the order in which each value is first encountered when scanning the first list followed by the second list. Either input list may be empty.

Write a function that returns the values that appear in exactly one of two lists (not both), each listed only once, with the qualifying values from the first list appearing first in their original order followed by the qualifying values from the second list in their original order. Either input list may be empty.
Write a function that returns the value that occurs most frequently in a non-empty list of integers. If two or more values are tied for the highest frequency, return the smallest such value.

Write a function that returns the k largest values from a list, sorted in descending order, including duplicates. If k is greater than or equal to the length of the list, return all elements sorted descending. If k is 0, return an empty list.

Write a function that sorts a list of numbers and then reorders it by alternately taking the smallest remaining value and the largest remaining value, starting with the smallest, until all elements are placed. The input list may be empty or contain duplicates.

Write a function that returns a new list with every nth element removed, using 1-based positions (so positions n, 2n, 3n, and so on are dropped), preserving the order of the remaining elements. Assume n is a positive integer; the input list may be empty.

Write a function that returns a new list containing only every nth element, using 1-based positions (so it keeps positions n, 2n, 3n, and so on), preserving their relative order. Assume n is a positive integer; the input list may be empty.

Write a function that returns a list of suffix sums where each output element is the sum of all input elements from that position to the end of the list (inclusive). The output has the same length as the input; an empty input returns an empty output.

Write a function that returns the running (cumulative) product of a list of numbers as a new list of the same length, where each output element is the product of all input elements up to and including that position. An empty input produces an empty output.

Write a function that subtracts the first element of a list from every element (including itself), returning a new list of the same length where the first entry is always 0. An empty input returns an empty output.
Write a function that counts how many times an element in a list is strictly greater than the element immediately following it (a descent). A list with fewer than 2 elements has 0 descents.
Write a function that counts how many times an element in a list is strictly less than the element immediately following it (an ascent). A list with fewer than 2 elements has 0 ascents.
